title: Jack Draper ends season early due to injury, targeting 2027 return to ATP Tour
content:
Jack Draper has said he will not play again in 2026 due to fatigue from a “complicated” injury and is targeting a return to the ATP Tour at the start of 2027.

The 24-year-old Briton, ranked No. 155 in the world, announced the decision on Instagram on Tuesday after being limited to 15 competitive singles matches this season by a chronic elbow injury in his left, playing arm and a separate right knee injury.

The former world No. 4 first experienced pain in his left elbow during the 2025 clay-court season and later developed serious bone bruising which forced him to withdraw from the U.S. Open after his first-round victory. He returned for Great Britain in the Davis Cup in February before making his ATP Tour comeback in Dubai later that month.

“Last summer all the dedication and work I had put into this sport was coming together,” Draper wrote. “It was all going my way and the path seemed so clear.

“However a complicated injury made things incredibly challenging and since that moment I’ve been desperately trying to get back and feel as I once did on the court. Managing so much change, adversity and pain has helped me to grow massively in many areas of my life but has also made me feel a level of fatigue.

“I am taking this time to reset and heal so when I return I am 100 per cent ready to go.”

Draper went on to reach the Indian Wells quarterfinals, beating Novak Djokovic before losing to Daniil Medvedev, but his comeback was interrupted in April when tendinitis in his right knee forced him to retire from his first-round match against Tomás Martín Etcheverry at the Barcelona Open.

The knee injury kept him out of the remainder of the clay-court season, including the French Open, before he returned at Eastbourne in June and reached the semifinals but withdrew from Wimbledon the following week after the bone bruising in his left arm recurred.

Another attempted comeback during the North American hard-court swing ended with first-round defeats at the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open in August. Draper was in tears during his loss to Térence Atmane in Montreal as the elbow problem appeared to flare again.

His defeat by Martín Landaluce in Cincinnati nine days later proved to be his final match of the year, meaning he did not play a Grand Slam match in 2026.
